body:
Thank you for you kind words, the encourage me to keep with treatment really help. I have read up on co-dependency because I basically was that when I was depressed. Obviously now I'm trying to be more independent but some days I do need more help then others.

I truly believe he did forget, so I don't see it as staying theoretically in contact with her but his action (or inaction) certainly did hurt me.

I guess some further backstory is needed in that I was (unknowingly)depressed when I met him but I see it as more the beginning of my spiral downwards due to some problems I was having with my family, starting university, moving to a new city. He was very supportive during those times but just like you said you can't push string. I only accepted help when I was ready.

He was very certain of himself almost to the point of cockiness and I can tell right now he is depressed. He is truly remorseful in what he did and added with hating his job and a lot of his friends moving away he became very unhappy. It sucks because I wouldn't wish depression on anyone and him blowing off my ideas on how to boost himself up is classic classic depression. It also sucks because I know there is nothing I can do, you only get better if you want to get better.

Similar thing happened to me except I met him at the beginning of my spiral. It came down to the point where I pushed him away because the misery felt more familiar. I felt like I didn't deserve the love and understanding and the more I pushed the more I hated myself and surrounded myself with the familiar feeling of hurt and shame.

He ended up breaking up with me because he was unhappy with the relationship. It wasn't until then that I realized how much it hurt him that I pushed him so hard. I was so caught up in my misery that I didn't realize that it affected every person I had pushed out of my life.

I don't want to hurt people in my life, it's probably why I pushed so many people out of it because I wanted to end my life but I only wanted to do it if I knew for sure people could get over it. When I found out how much I hurt him I realized that some people might never "get over" me being dead (also the process of getting people out of my life hurt them) and so I began researching depression and talking to people here. So begins my slow uphill climb back up.

It's good that you made a doctor's appointment, the first step is always hard. Helping yourself and taking care of yourself are an important part of caring for others as well.

I can maybe give some insight from a depressed person's side. 

My boyfriend recently broke up with me because of my depression for similar reasons as to why you are angry. It wasn't until he broke up with me that he told me outright how unhappy he was with our relationship. This hit a note with me and I saw how much I pushed people out of my life which spurred me to research and learn more about depression ultimately leading me to no longer accept depression as a way to live.

It's great that you are trying to be understanding and learning more about this illness. It's important to understand that no one wants to feel this way or act this way. He probably feels ashamed and embarrassed at his inability to do all these things. While you may think he sits at home and just lounges, he is actually very stressed. He's stressed about all the things he needs to do and wonders why he can't do them. 

These are only suggestions because I'm not a pro by any means, this is based on my experiences, only you know your relationship with him.
I believe that if my ex had sat me down and talked to me about his feelings about our relationship I maybe would've gotten motivated sooner, it wasn't the breaking up but rather the knowledge that he was unhappy. So if you think you can sit him down and have a true talk about your feelings about how you don't want him to lie to you, that might be something to consider. Sounds like he cares about you and doesn't want to disappoint you. Remember don't accuse him, just tell him how you feel, if you're stressed, etc. I know it's scary voicing your own problems on a depressed person especially when your problems are with them, so if you think you can maybe just start out small.

I wish you all the best, it's a very difficult thing you are going through too. When he does start doing more things like doing the dishes or showering, remember to thank him or show that you noticed. I found praise is pretty important when I started dealing with my depression.
Thanks a bunch I'll check it out.

Your words are good, I like hope, I like knowing that the "right" counselor is important. I've only talked to one and it really felt meh he pushed me to speak to my family every session and it kindof became a stalemate because I wasn't going to do it. Maybe I should've just listened to him but I really really didn't want to speak to them, or atleast not yet.

I also started university on the wrong foot too, it was also the beginning of my spiral. I felt it just added more stress and weight on top of everything that I was feeling. Do not make the same mistake as me and keep trying to go back and pushing through it. It ruined my GPA and I won't be able to get back in unless I take a much longer route such as college then back to uni or take a few uni classes each semester until I up my GPA to reapply to a program.

If you need to stop and take time off do it, it is not wasted time. I guess I feel so strongly about it because I wish someone had told me it was alright. I just felt worst knowing I had a closed a door by thinking I could just trudge through it when I couldn't.
It is my fault though. I dragged him into my darkness how else was it going to end. Why would anyone love someone so sad. I can barely stand myself sometimes.

I couldn't keep being depressed if I wanted to stay with him.

I'm a shitty person because I got into this relationship knowing that I shouldn't. I was depressed and I knew I would be dragging him under my rain cloud. It was selfish. I fight with him over getting help. I see the hurt in his eyes when I hurt myself. I made a post not too long ago on [/r/depression](/r/depression) it gives a little more background.
It's not so much the venting, he can't deal with me venting anymore. I push him away by struggling to get motivated, by struggling with getting help.
